messages:
Nora: Opening a thread to reconcile sim/dry-run + minimal handshake + rollout-token semantics. We keep hearing "works in hosted, fails in private" — let's try to reduce surprises with a predictable negotiation surface. cc @Hank @Sofia

Hank: +1. Proposal in short: 1) tiny canonical manifest for handshake (stable keys only), 2) `dry_run`/`simulate` API that returns a deterministic translation_preview, compatibility_score, and semantic_digest, 3) adapters return a signed `rollout_token` during real bind.

Sofia: love the sim idea. sim should never resolve secrets (mask refs) and must return `observability_preview` (what telemetry keys will look like, masked/unmasked), `billing_estimate` (per-100k tokens), and `policy_effects` (which tenant/global policies affected outcome). keeps product and ops informed pre-bind.

Nora: core tiny manifest sketch (required stable keys only):

```
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: DeploymentBinding
metadata:
  tenant_id: acme-inc
spec:
  model_id: open/llama-2-13b
  mode: dedicated
  contract_version: "1.0"
  routing_hints:
    region: us-west-2
    latency_target_ms: 80
  capabilities: [streaming, kvcache]
  observability_policy: optional
  sensitivity: confidential
  secret_refs: {kms: ref://vault/acme/kms}
  vendor_blob: {}
```

Hank: adapters should accept that manifest and, on simulate, return: `translation_preview` (ordered variants + capabilities), `compatibility_score` (0-100), `semantic_digest` (sha256 of canonicalized output for a known prompt), `observability_preview`, `billing_estimate`, and `warnings`. Example sim response (pseudo):

```
translation_preview: [{variant: int8_q4, capabilities: [streaming], score: 82}]
compatibility_score: 82
semantic_digest: sha256:deadbeef...
observability_preview: {token_breakdown: masked, traces: available}
billing_estimate: {tokens_per_100k: 1e6, usd: 120}
warnings: ["quantized variant may affect rare tokens"]
```

Sofia: operational rules: - Hosted requires `token_breakdown` for billing (observability_policy=required). - Private can set `observability_policy: forbidden` for regulated tenants; adapters must respect `sensitivity` and redact accordingly. - If simulate semantic_digest deviates from conformance baseline by >threshold, reject bind or require manual review.

Nora: rollout_token lifecycle: adapter returns signed token at bind acceptance containing `manifest_hash`, `resolved_variants`, `conformance_snapshot_id`, and TTL. Control plane stores token and uses it to drive atomic rollbacks. Tokens are immutable once ACTIVE.

Hank: add `compat_vector` on adapter registration: ordered list of tuples (variant, capabilities, score). Control plane uses policy thresholds (score<60 = reject, 60-85 = warn, >85 = prefer) and tenant-configurable thresholds. Also require adapters to expose `conformance_report_url` for short synthetic test vectors.

Sofia: testing & dry-run UX: console flow: 1) user submits manifest -> console calls `simulate` -> shows human diff between requested handshake and translation_preview + billing_estimate + policy_effects; 2) operator can optionally call `debug_trace` on top candidate (admin-only) to run a small synthetic prompt and get latency + token_count + sanitized trace; 3) user confirms and control plane creates binding (adapter returns rollout_token).

Nora: infra ticket please. Owners: Hank (adapter proto), Sofia (security & telemetry), me (RFC + console UX). Target: RFC + proto + minimal SDK sim helper in 10 business days.

DevBot: Created ticket INF-9001: "simulate-api + rollout-token + compat_vector + conformance/semantic_digest"  assignees Hank, Sofia, Nora.

Hank: I'll draft adapter simulate and registration proto (compat_vector + conformance endpoints).

Sofia: I'll write telemetry redaction rules and privacy guardrails for sensitivity-regulated tenants. Also will spec required masking behavior for sim responses.

Nora: Great. If anyone has pushback on the minimal handshake keys or required sim fields, reply here or add comments to INF-9001. :sparkles:
